title: After the Church Rock spill
text: After the Church Rock uranium spill, the Navajo Nation asked New Mexico's governor to declare a state of emergency and to seek a federal disaster declaration. The governor said no. A warning sign posted along the Puerco River after the spill told residents, in English, Spanish, and Diné, to stay away from the water. The mill was allowed to start up again within months of the spill, and in 1983 the site was put on the national Superfund priority list.

s2.title: Tragedy at Church Rock: Superfunds and the Marginalization of Navajos
s2.publisher: Intermountain Histories (Sam Heywood, Brigham Young University)
s2.quote: the Navajo Nation appealed to the state’s governor to declare a state of emergency in the Church Rock area, a request that was denied. ... the state and federal government quickly complied to let mill operations resume just five months after the massive spill. ... landed the Church Rock on the National Priority List for Superfund sites in 1983.

s3.title: On Poisoned Ground
s3.publisher: Science History Institute (Linda M. Richards, April 22, 2013)
s3.quote: A sign along the Rio Puerco warns residents in English, Spanish, and Diné to avoid the water in Church Rock, New Mexico. Warnings were posted after the July 16, 1979, United Nuclear Corporation's uranium tailings spill.
